topIssues.title: [Epic] Ship the agentic parent suite with trustworthy household coordination
topIssues.author: lalalune
topIssues.body:
## Goal

Ship a trustworthy LifeOps parent-assistant suite that materially reduces the
anticipation, planning, coordination, monitoring, and recovery work carried by
a busy world-traveling mother coordinating children with a co-parent and
caregivers.

The completed system must ingest authoritative household sources, reason over
multiple calendars without leaking private event details, distinguish proposals
from agreements, obtain the right approvals, monitor material changes, execute
typed transactions exactly once, and verify closure. It must expose source
freshness and errors instead of presenting unavailable data as a healthy empty
state.

## Design doc

`packages/docs/ongoing-development/research/11-agentic-parent-suite.md`

## Scope

- Calendar source registry, sync health, multi-account aggregation, guest
  free/busy, ICS/webcal, and Microsoft Graph calendar support.
- Deterministic conflict/availability evaluation for time, people, custody,
  caregivers, transport, locations, resources, travel, recurrence, time zones,
  DST, and all-day events.
- Typed schedule proposals, per-party agreements, material-change
  invalidation, approval-gated messaging, and provider materialization.
- Household roles, scoped/expiring caregiver access, private-busy projection,
  append-only audit, and scoped export.
- School/activity ingestion and correction monitoring; action bundles,
  responsibility ownership, seasonal opportunities, household items, and
  external-source adapters.
- Food constraints, inventory confidence, cart/order idempotency, delivery
  exception recovery, childcare/work modeling, and source-grounded parenting
  guidance with human handoff.
- A composite world-traveling co-parent persona plus G1-G48 capability
  scenarios, real-provider tests, live-model trajectories, and manually
  reviewed evidence.

## Non-goals

- A second scheduler, household graph, connector abstraction, or file store.
- Behavior keyed from prompt text or demographic runtime modes.
- Autonomous sensitive messages, custody changes, medical/legal decisions, or
  purchases without typed policy and required approval.
- Scraping private guest calendars or fabricating availability, inventory,
  costs, source health, transactions, or completion.

## Work Items

- [ ] Ratify calendar-source health, proposal/agreement, access, audit,
      responsibility, provenance, and transaction contracts.
- [ ] Consolidate conflict detection and wire production guest free/busy.
- [ ] Route scheduling lifecycle communication through draft and approval
      policy.
- [ ] Implement provider-neutral sync, pagination, cursors, webhooks, and
      idempotent reconciliation.
- [ ] Implement Microsoft and hardened ICS/webcal sources.
- [ ] Implement household roles, scoped access, private-busy, audit, and export.
- [ ] Implement schedule proposals, approvals, materiality, and final
      calendar materialization.
- [ ] Implement school/activity ingestion, correction monitoring, action
      bundles, and weekly responsibility review.
- [ ] Implement weather/maps/local-activity sources and seasonal/household
      item workflows.
- [ ] Implement food, inventory, cart, order, refund, and delivery-recovery
      workflows.
- [ ] Implement deterministic childcare/work scenarios and source-grounded
      parenting guidance boundaries.
- [ ] Author and live-verify G1-G48 plus all ten Jordan co-parent scenarios.
- [ ] Reconcile every overlapping open LifeOps issue and PR; reuse valid work
      and close no item until the production path and evidence are complete.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] Every row in the design doc delivery ledger is complete.
- [ ] The busy world-traveling co-parent journey works from source ingestion
      through conflict discovery, privacy-preserving coordination, approval,
      materialization, change recovery, and closure.
- [ ] Loading, designed-empty, unavailable, stale, partial, and error states are
      distinguishable at every source boundary.
- [ ] No private event title, child-private fact, or unrelated adult data leaks
      across household scopes or exports.
- [ ] Duplicate/out-of-order provider events, retries, concurrent approvals,
      recurrence edits, DST/date-line crossings, and transaction retries are
      deterministic and idempotent.
- [ ] Real-provider or sandbox-provider contracts cover every connector; mocks
      and deterministic LLM fixtures are supplemental only.
- [ ] Live-model scenarios record inputs, provider context, actions, outputs,
      and domain artifacts, and every artifact is manually reviewed.
- [ ] Full package tests, repository verification, and all applicable UI,
      security, and evidence gates pass after rebasing on `origin/develop`.

## Evidence Plan

- [ ] Screenshots or recording: full desktop/mobile flow where UI applies;
      otherwise an explicit N/A reason per backend-only work item.
- [ ] Logs: structured backend logs plus frontend console/network logs where UI
      applies, including success, partial-source, stale, permission, and recovery
      paths.
- [ ] Real-LLM trajectories: JSON report, run viewer, and native JSONL for the
      persona and adversarial corpus, opened and reviewed by hand.
- [ ] Domain artifacts: calendar events/provider IDs, approvals, proposals,
      access grants, audit events/exports, source versions, scheduled tasks,
      carts/orders/receipts/refunds, and completion records.
- [ ] CI runs: scoped package lanes, full `bun run verify`, relevant real E2E
      lanes, and all PR checks.

## Dependencies / Sequencing

- Project: <https://github.com/orgs/elizaOS/projects/15>
- Coordination: <https://github.com/orgs/elizaOS/discussions/14407>
- Persona and journey workstream: <https://github.com/orgs/elizaOS/discussions/14392>
- Process and evidence workstream: <https://github.com/orgs/elizaOS/discussions/14406>
- Existing co-parent E2E: #14789
- Relationship inference/capture: #14785 and #14786
- Scheduling output proof: #14874
- Multi-account source ingestion: #14758 and #14792
- Existing LifeOps live verification: #16938 and #16941
- Side-effect receipts and final send-boundary proof: #17027

Sequence the truth and authorization layers before new convenience domains:
calendar/source health → proposals/access/audit → school/household sources →
food/transactions → financial/guidance surfaces → complete live persona proof.

topIssues.title: fix(cloud): make large-agent image upgrades rollback-safe without hydrating shared Postgres
topIssues.author: NubsCarson
topIssues.body:
## Problem

The production admin-canary upgrade for the demo agent failed safely before cutover because the mandatory pre-upgrade snapshot exceeded the Cloud raw hydration budget:

- production deploy: `main@054fc9feff4f95dc97409cc7b703e2e45600ebcc`
- canary workflow: `30183809168`
- canary job: `771bc989-3244-41d7-bb03-c9ff565be8c6`
- sanitized actor-bound cause: `Pre-upgrade snapshot failed: Snapshot payload exceeds the raw hydration budget (268435456 bytes) — refusing to retain it`

The current v1 agent snapshot eagerly materializes one JSON document containing every agent-owned shared-Postgres row, including derived embeddings, plus base64 local files. Cloud accepts up to 256 MiB, while `/api/restore` and backup-chain reconstruction cap at 128 MiB, so a 128–256 MiB snapshot can authorize a cutover but be impossible to restore. R2 offload happens only after the whole payload has already been downloaded, parsed, reserialized, encrypted, and retained.

For managed Cloud agents, old and new containers use the same external Postgres database. Copying that database into the container snapshot is both wasteful and semantically dangerous: the current rollback restore deletes/reinserts live shared rows while the current image may still be serving.

This extends #16639; it is the rollout-blocking correctness closure discovered by the exact production canary.

## Required architecture

### 1. Immediate v1 safety alignment

- Define one canonical v1 maximum restorable wire size shared by agent restore, Cloud fetch, backup reconstruction, and verification; it must not exceed 128 MiB.
- Add source-side aggregate/raw/expanded budgeting so the agent aborts before eagerly retaining every component.
- Budget failures are typed, observable, privacy-safe, non-retryable, and occur before cutover.
- Keep manual/auto v1 behavior for genuinely small backups; do not raise heap or body limits.

### 2. Legacy-to-v2 standby bridge

The first rollout crosses an image-protocol boundary: the old image emits only v1 and rejects a v2 database reference. A projected v1 payload cannot make old restore safe because an empty/partial `postgres-rows` restore deletes data.

- Add a distinct durable legacy-standby lifecycle; do not reuse `replacement_cleanup_*`, whose reconciler semantics mean “garbage to destroy.”
- After the new image is provisioned and healthy, stop-preserve the exact old container, volume, VPN identity, image digest, environment generation, and capacity ownership.
- Atomically cut traffic to the new placement while retaining the old stopped container as rollback authority.
- Any failed acceptance CAS-switches back to that exact standby without calling old `/api/restore`.
- Standby retirement requires a verified v2 restore point and explicit acceptance; time alone may never retire it.
- Recovery/reconciliation must be crash-safe and generation/CAS fenced.

### 3. Additive v2 backup protocol

- `POST /api/snapshot` accepts a bounded purpose/capability contract.
- Shared/BYO Postgres is represented by a credential-free, agent-bound connection-identity fingerprint/reference; restore requires an exact match and performs zero SQL deletes/inserts.
- PGlite remains a real captured/restored database component.
- Local media, vault, character/config, and state are streamed as deterministic bounded archive chunks.
- Reuse `agent_sandbox_backups` and the existing tenant-scoped backup namespace. Store an encrypted descriptor plus chunk objects; do not introduce a second backup store.
- Each fixed-size chunk uses authenticated encryption with AAD binding organization, sandbox, backup, schema, index, and size. Hashes/nonces/tags live in the descriptor; commit the descriptor only after every chunk verifies.
- Restore streams, decrypts, verifies, and stages all components before destructive apply. Reject traversal, symlinks, malformed/truncated streams, wrong tenant/agent/database identity, and partial data.
- Reconcile the required R2 bindings into the provisioning daemon. Existing whole-string object helpers must not carry v2.

### 4. Rollout

- Prefer a narrow bridge image first, then the feature image, so rollback-protocol risk is isolated.
- The first legacy→v2 canary retains the old standby through real v2 restore proof.
- After the v2 image becomes the declared rollback floor, subsequent blue/green upgrades use v2 backups and the ordinary cleanup path.
- Never bypass the mandatory restore point, silently drop local state, or treat the external-Postgres reference as a disaster backup.

## Acceptance and evidence

- [ ] Exact-limit v1 passes; limit+1 fails before cutover; Cloud and restore limits cannot diverge.
- [ ] Source-side snapshot collection stays bounded and cancels promptly.
- [ ] A >256 MiB legacy fixture crosses the protocol boundary with bounded worker memory while the old standby remains rollback-capable.
- [ ] Crash/retry at every standby phase converges exactly once without destroying the serving or rollback placement.
- [ ] Failed acceptance CAS-restores the exact old standby without `/api/restore`.
- [ ] v2 shared-Postgres restore validates identity, issues zero SQL, and preserves rows written after snapshot.
- [ ] PGlite, media, vault, character/config, and state round-trip exactly, including corrupt/truncated/adversarial cases.
- [ ] No backup descriptor becomes visible until every encrypted chunk is durable and verified; orphan chunks are reconciled safely.
- [ ] Existing small v1 manual backup/restore remains green.
- [ ] Real production canary succeeds for the exact published digest, then proves `/api/health` zero failed plugins, Cerebras chat, Notes/Calendar create/show/edit/switch/delete, restart persistence, PWA, and physical LP3.
- [ ] Structured backend logs, memory/stream metrics, exact SHAs/digests, real HTTP evidence, browser/device screenshots, and a walkthrough are attached and reviewed.

## Rejected shortcuts

Raising payload/heap limits, gzip-only wrapping, raw JSON-to-R2 after hydration, empty/partial Postgres v1 dumps, skipping rollback, same-node volume assumptions, or destroying the old container before acceptance.

topPRs.title: fix(cloud): recover stale managed canaries safely
topPRs.author: NubsCarson
topPRs.body:
## Summary

- add an authenticated, organization-scoped conditional Eliza-agent DELETE contract that owns an exact name, creation timestamp, and execution tier under the existing lifecycle advisory lock
- fail closed around replacement cleanup, warm claims, in-progress work, retry ownership, and recent detached lifecycle execution; only quiescent stale work may be cancelled before the exact CAS
- recover the one explicitly supplied stale managed-canary suffix through normal GET/DELETE/job APIs, then require final 404 proof before provisioning a fresh canary
- bind recovery intent into workflow dispatch evidence and keep the evidence schema privacy-safe

## Why

The staging managed-dedicated canary is blocked by one old exact canary row from run 30081355987. Generic deletion, direct database edits, and prefix-wide cleanup are unsafe. This change provides a bounded exact-identity recovery path without weakening deployment or environment protections.

Refs #17158

## Proof

- bun run test:cloud — all 11 batches passed, 0 failures
- bun run verify:cloud — 85/85 tasks passed
- bun run verify — 578/578 lint/typecheck tasks plus all repository audits and 28 dist-path consumer checks passed
- bun run build:cloud — passed
- bun run build:core — 71/71 tasks passed
- focused canary/workflow tests — 48 passed, 0 failed
- API DELETE route tests — 6 passed, 0 failed
- focused Cloud shared real-PGlite lifecycle tests — 37 passed, 0 failed
- production Worker dry-run — passed
- git diff --check — clean
- independent blocker review — APPROVED, no remaining P0/P1

## Safety invariants

- no direct database mutation or ad-hoc host/container cleanup
- no broad prefix delete
- no token or suffix disclosure in artifacts
- no second provision while a known provision job is still nonterminal
- no environment-policy change or self-approval bypass
- normal no-body/whitespace DELETE behavior remains backward compatible

## UI evidence

N/A — no UI or renderer path changed.

## Post-merge rollout

1. Deploy the exact merge SHA to staging API and provisioning worker.
2. Dispatch one sanctioned staging canary with stale suffix r30081355987a1.
3. Require recovery confirmation, fresh canary proof, cleanup confirmation, and terminal green.
4. Only then selectively backport the exact proven change to production and repeat the protected canary before physical LP3 Notes/Calendar validation.

topPRs.title: fix(cloud): diagnose stale canary deletes safely
topPRs.author: NubsCarson
topPRs.body:
## Summary

- add a workflow-dispatch-only, staging-only read-only diagnostic for one exact managed-canary suffix
- query exactly one sandbox plus its three newest `agent_delete` jobs inside `BEGIN READ ONLY`, with `default_transaction_read_only=on`, a 20-second statement cap, and a step-scoped database credential
- convert the private raw row into a mode-0600 strict allowlist containing only statuses, counts, booleans, classified failure codes, and timestamps/durations
- reject unknown shapes/text, non-inline payloads, contradictory lifecycle state, zero/multiple targets, and any output containing identifier/URL/IP/secret patterns
- leave the normal schedule, labeled-PR, and manual canary path unchanged unless the explicit diagnostic input is selected

## Why

The exact post-merge staging recovery canary for #17173 (run 30224564063, deployed commit `e00283274bd6490f6fedc02fd56f9de92dbe29fd`) found one stale dedicated canary and received `202` for its identity-bound delete, but the async `agent_delete` exhausted three attempts after 200.9 seconds. The public artifact correctly collapses private job details to `job_failed`; a blind retry is unsafe until operators know whether the failure happened before or after provider-side slot release.

Closes #17184

## Proof

- focused diagnostic tests — 16 passed, 0 failed
- executable privacy/shape tests — unknown raw errors, identifiers, non-inline payloads, mismatched retry results, row-delete classification, terminal duration, semantic contradictions, exact CLI wiring
- `actionlint .github/workflows/managed-dedicated-canary.yml` — passed
- Biome exact two TypeScript files — passed
- `git diff --check` — clean
- independent workflow/security review — no P0 or code-path P1; merge-first dispatch required by the existing develop-only staging environment rule
- error-policy ratchet — N/A: the exact base does not contain the named audit script; the new production file adds no catch or console usage

## Safety invariants

- no POST, DELETE, UPDATE, INSERT, DDL, host SSH, provider call, or canary creation
- no environment-policy change; dispatch occurs only after merge from exact `develop`
- database credential exists only in the SQL step and is absent from tests, transformer, upload, and summary
- both client default and explicit SQL transaction are read-only
- raw database JSON stays mode-0600 on the ephemeral runner and is deleted before upload
- no IDs, names, suffixes, org/user data, database strings, hosts, URLs, IPs, digests, credentials, or raw errors enter the artifact/summary
- production is untouched

## Post-merge proof

1. Dispatch exact suffix `r30081355987a1` from merged `develop`.
2. Require exactly one target and a privacy-safe terminal job classification.
3. Decide source repair versus sanctioned retry from that packet; do not rerun deletion blindly.

Closes #17170. Extracted from the still-valid core portion of #16591.

## Summary

Adds the typed, browser-safe core resolver for canonical small/large model slots and exports it consistently from Node, browser, and edge entrypoints.

This is deliberately only the foundation. It does not wire providers, CLI inference, host seeding/display, or Cloud configuration.

## Contract

- Runtime setting outranks injected environment.
- Blank runtime values defer to environment.
- Explicit malformed/mistyped runtime values fail closed.
- Known family qualifications are accepted only for the matching family.
- Native slash IDs and family-pinned slash IDs remain intact.
- Empty, control-character, double-known-prefix, and unknown-caller-family inputs are rejected.

topPRs.title: fix(cloud): bound the v1 snapshot retain budget by what restore can consume (#17172 §1)
topPRs.author: standujar
topPRs.body:
# Relates to

Implements **#17172 §1 only** ("Immediate v1 safety alignment"). §2–4 (legacy standby bridge, additive v2 backup protocol, rollout) are deliberately **out of scope** — that is the larger architecture the card's owner should keep. Claimed on-issue with that scope before starting.

Definition of Done: full standard in [`CONTRIBUTING.md`](../CONTRIBUTING.md).

- [x] This PR targets `develop` and is rebased onto the latest `origin/develop` with zero conflicts.
- [x] `bun install` and `bun run verify` were run after sync, or any failure is recorded below with the exact unrelated blocker.
- [x] A reviewer can confirm the change works without reading the code, from the evidence attached below.

# Sync with develop

- [x] Branched from the latest `origin/develop`; zero conflicts.
- [x] Targeted verification recorded under **Testing** (changed-package tests + typecheck).

# Risks

Low, and strictly in the safe direction: the retain budget only ever gets **smaller** (256 MiB → 128 MiB), never larger. Nothing that restores today stops restoring; what stops is retaining a payload that could never be restored. Small manual/auto v1 backups are untouched, and no heap or body limit is raised (the issue's rejected-shortcuts list is respected).

# Background

## What does this PR do?

The production canary failed because Cloud **retained** a snapshot larger than anything on the restore path can **consume**:

| Side | Constant | Before | After |
|---|---|---|---|
| retain | `SNAPSHOT_MAX_RAW_BYTES` (`eliza-sandbox.ts`) | **256 MiB** | canonical (128 MiB), env-clamped |
| restore | `MAX_BACKUP_BODY_BYTES` (`packages/agent/src/api/server.ts`) | 128 MiB | canonical |
| reconstruct | `MAX_RECONSTRUCTED_BACKUP_CHAIN_BYTES` (`agent-sandboxes.ts`) | 128 MiB | canonical |

A 128–256 MiB snapshot was therefore retained, authorized a cutover, and could never be restored.

- New `packages/shared/src/agent-backup-limits.ts` holds **`MAX_RESTORABLE_AGENT_BACKUP_BYTES` (128 MiB)** — the one canonical v1 restorable wire size. `@elizaos/shared` is already a dependency of **both** `packages/agent` and `packages/cloud/shared`, so retain, restore and reconstruction import one source of truth with no import cycle. This mirrors the existing `chat-upload-limits.ts` precedent (a leaf limits module both sides import so they cannot drift).
- `resolveRetainableAgentBackupBytes()` resolves the `ELIZA_SNAPSHOT_MAX_RAW_BYTES` operator override **clamped to the canonical limit**. The override keeps its real purpose (lowering the budget for a staging soak or a constrained worker) but can no longer re-open the divergence by configuration alone — which it could before.
- The breach still fails exactly where it already did: **while streaming, before retention** (`readBodyWithinBudget`), so a too-large snapshot is never persisted and never authorizes a cutover.

## Deliberately NOT changed: the verifier's decrypt budget

`DEFAULT_MAX_DECRYPT_BYTES` (256 MiB, `agent-backup-verifier.ts`) is left alone on purpose. It is a **per-cycle aggregate** budget spanning a batch of backups, not a per-backup wire size — a different axis. Lowering it to 128 MiB would be a *regression*: one max-size backup would consume an entire cycle, so the sweep would verify a single backup per cycle. At 256 MiB a max-size (128 MiB) backup always fits with room to spare, and `chargeBudget` already distinguishes `payload-exceeds-cycle-budget` (permanent, stop sampling) from `cycle-budget-exhausted` (transient, defer) — so the "can never verify" case is already handled correctly.

## What kind of change is this?

Bug fix (correctness: removes a retainable-but-unrestorable backup state).

# Documentation changes needed?

My changes do not require a change to the project documentation; the new module documents the contract at its definition.

# Testing

## Where should a reviewer start?

`packages/shared/src/agent-backup-limits.test.ts` — it pins the whole contract: the canonical ceiling is 128 MiB; an override that **lowers** is honored; an override that **raises** (including the exact pre-fix 256 MiB that produced the unrestorable canary snapshot) is clamped; malformed/non-positive fall back; exact-limit passes and limit+1 clamps; and a final invariant case asserting no input can ever resolve a retain budget above the restorable ceiling — the guard that fails if someone raises one side without the other.

## Detailed testing steps

None: automated tests are acceptable. `packages/shared` vitest lane: **7 pass / 0 fail** on the new suite. The pre-existing budget tests in `eliza-sandbox.test.ts` (from #16639/#16647) pass explicit budgets into `readBodyWithinBudget`/`assertSnapshotExpandedBudgets`, so they are unaffected by the default change.

# Evidence Details

The load-bearing new property is the **clamp**, not the constant: before this PR an operator could set `ELIZA_SNAPSHOT_MAX_RAW_BYTES=268435456` and silently recreate the exact canary failure. The test asserts that specific value now resolves to the canonical 128 MiB, plus a general invariant over a range of inputs so the property holds for anything an operator types.

## Known gaps / failures

Only §1 of #17172 is addressed — §2 (legacy→v2 standby bridge), §3 (additive v2 chunked backup protocol) and §4 (rollout) remain open on the card and are the substantial architecture. This PR makes the current v1 path *safe* (no unrestorable retention) but does not make large agents *backupable* — a >128 MiB agent will now fail cleanly before cutover instead of retaining a dead snapshot, which is the intended §1 behavior ("budget failures are typed, observable, non-retryable, and occur before cutover") and exactly why §3 exists.
